blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising sequences of ordinary vocabulary tokens, any of which may be corrupted and subsequently revised. During training, UDLMs must denoise from a context that may itself be unreliable, whereas masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) always condition on a clean context. This challenging training objective makes UDLMs more FLOP-intensive to train than MDLMs, but it yields stronger downstream reasoning performance. Recently, selective looping, which recursively applies a few early Transformer layers within each denoising step, has been shown to improve training efficiency in MDLMs under an iso-FLOP budget. We investigate looping in UDLMs while keeping the training objective and sampler unchanged. We find that looping significantly improves training efficiency: looped UDLMs reach the validation NLL of a non-looped UDLM trained on about 0.5 trillion tokens with up to 2.8x fewer training FLOPs on OpenWebText and 3.3x fewer on FineWeb-Edu. We also find that, at a matched NFE budget, looped UDLMs reach up to 9.8% lower generation perplexity than the non-looped UDLM, with most gains achieved at moderate loop counts. Finally, we study different loop-count distributions and find that sampling smaller loop counts more frequently during training improves inference efficiency: on downstream tasks, this strategy uses 12% fewer loops than uniform loop-count sampling without degrading accuracy.

blocks.en:
Discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate text by starting from a
corrupted sequence and denoising many positions in
parallel ( Austin et al., 2021 ; Lou et al., 2024 ; Sahoo et al., 2024 ; Nie et al., 2025 ; Lai et al., 2025 ) .
The forward process decides whether the denoiser knows which tokens are
corrupted. Masked diffusion language
models (MDLMs) replace corrupted tokens with a dedicated mask symbol, so the
corrupted positions are always known. Under the standard absorbing-state
reverse process, unmasked tokens are never
changed ( Sahoo et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2024 ; Ou et al., 2025 ; Zheng et al., 2025 ) . Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) instead replace tokens with
random tokens from the vocabulary, so every position holds an ordinary token
that gives no sign of being
corrupted ( Austin et al., 2021 ; Schiff et al., 2025 ; Sahoo et al., 2025 ; Hong et al., 2026 ) .
Because of this, the reverse process can revise any position at any denoising
step. The distinction is becoming more important as uniform diffusion is
scaled to billion-parameter language models for
reasoning ( DiffusionGemma Team et al., 2026 ; Sahoo et al., 2026a ) .

blocks.en:
Denoising in UDLMs is harder than in MDLMs because the denoiser must predict corrupted tokens from a context that may itself be corrupted. If a token does not fit its context, either the token or one of its neighbors was corrupted, and the denoiser has to work out which. At each position it therefore predicts two things. The first is the probability that the observed token was retained, which depends on the noise level and on how well the token agrees with its context. The second is the clean token itself, in case it was
replaced. Both are read from the model’s contextual prediction of the clean token, so refining that prediction should improve both. The most
straightforward way to refine it is to scale up the model by adding layers, but this increases the parameter count. Another way is looping , which spends more computation on the same
noisy sequence by reusing existing layers, without adding
parameters ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ; Lan et al., 2020 ; Giannou et al., 2023 ; Geiping et al., 2025 ) . Lee et al. (2026) recently showed that selectively looping a small block
of early-middle layers improves training efficiency in MDLMs, where
unresolved positions are explicitly identified. Whether looping also helps
UDLMs, where the denoiser cannot tell which positions are corrupted, remains
open.
We therefore ask: How useful is looping for UDLM denoising, and how does the
loop-count distribution affect training and inference?

blocks.en: To investigate this question, we integrate looping into UDLMs while keeping the training objective and sampler unchanged, using Duo ++ ( Deschenaux et al., 2026 ) , the most efficient recipe for training UDLMs in the literature. Besides the uniform loop-count distribution used in prior work on looped masked diffusion ( Lee et al., 2026 ) , we study two alternatives: FLOP-proportional sampling, which gives each loop count the same expected share of training FLOPs, so smaller loop counts are sampled more often, and noise-proportional sampling, which assigns larger loop counts to noisier inputs. At inference, we consider fixed looping, which uses the same loop count at every denoising step, and adaptive looping, which halts once the relative change in the hidden state between consecutive iterations falls below a threshold.
blocks.zh: 为了调查这个问题,我们利用Duo ++将循环并入UDLM,同时保持培训目标和取样器不变。 (Deschenaux等人,2026年),是培养文学界UDLM的最有效配方. 除了在之前的循环遮掩扩散工作(Lee et al., 2026)中使用的统一循环计数分配法外,我们研究了两种替代方法:FLOP-比例抽样法,使每个循环计数在训练FLOP中得到相同的预期份额,因此较小的循环计数被比较频繁地采样,噪声-比例抽样法,将更大的循环计数分配给了鼻音输入法. 推论中,我们考虑固定循环,在每个去诺步骤使用相同的循环计数,以及适应性循环,一旦连续迭代之间隐藏状态的相对变化低于阈值,则停止循环.

blocks.en:
We summarize our observations as follows: 1. Looping makes UDLM training more compute-efficient. Looped UDLMs reach the validation NLL of a non-looped UDLM trained on
about 0.5 0.5 trillion tokens with up to 2.8 × 2.8\times fewer training FLOPs on OpenWebText ( Gokaslan and Cohen, 2019 ) and 3.3 × 3.3\times fewer on FineWeb-Edu ( Penedo et al., 2024 ) . 2. Looping helps at inference. Looped UDLMs reach up to 9.8 % 9.8\% lower generative perplexity than the non-looped UDLM at the same number of denoising steps, with most of the gain captured at moderate loop counts. On seven out-of-domain datasets, looping at inference lowers the zero-shot perplexity of the non-looped UDLM by 11.5 % 11.5\% on average. 3. Loops mainly refine predictions at replaced tokens. Extra loop iterations mostly improve the predicted clean token at replaced positions, not the choice of which tokens to keep. The gain is largest at intermediate noise. 4. Adaptive looping saves loop iterations without losing accuracy. On ten zero-shot multiple-choice tasks, adaptive looping matches the accuracy of twelve fixed loop iterations while running 26.0 % 26.0\% fewer of them with uniform sampling and 34.8 % 34.8\% fewer with FLOP-proportional sampling.

blocks.en:
The corruption process of UDLMs makes training challenging, because tokens
must be predicted from an unreliable context.
Concretely, a UDLM needs more training FLOPs than an MDLM to reach the same
validation NLL ( Sahoo et al., 2026b ) . Recent works have shown that looping,
which repeatedly applies a shared set of Transformer layers, adds depth
without adding parameters ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ; Giannou et al., 2023 ; Geiping et al., 2025 ) and improves the training efficiency of masked diffusion language models at
matched training FLOPs ( Lee et al., 2026 ) . Motivated by this, we
study the effect of looping on the training efficiency and downstream
performance of UDLMs, keeping the corruption process, the Duo ++ objective, and the sampler unchanged.
§ 3.1 quantifies the uncertainty created by
uniform corruption, and § 3.2 introduces the looped UDLM
denoiser and the loop-count distributions used to train it.

blocks.en: 6 Related Work
blocks.zh: 6 相关工作

blocks.en:
Discrete diffusion models use structured categorical corruption ( Austin et al., 2021 ; Hoogeboom et al., 2021 ) , with much of the
literature focusing on masked diffusion ( Sahoo et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2024 ; Ou et al., 2025 ; Lou et al., 2024 ; Nie et al., 2025 ) .
UDLMs instead corrupt tokens into ordinary vocabulary tokens,
allowing previously generated tokens to be revised ( Schiff et al., 2025 ; Sahoo et al., 2025 ; Sahoo et al., 2026b ) .
Existing acceleration methods largely reduce the number of
denoising steps through improved sampling or distillation ( Song et al., 2023 ; Kim et al., 2024 ; Hu et al., 2026 ; Peng et al., 2025 ; Israel et al., 2025 ; Luxembourg et al., 2025 ; Dang et al., 2025 ) .
Our work instead studies recurrent computation within each
denoising step, leaving the diffusion objective and sampler unchanged.
blocks.zh:
分散传播模式使用结构化的绝对腐败(Austin等人,2021年;Hoogeboom等人,2021年),其中多数为腐败。

我们的工作是研究每件事的反复计算
消除步骤,使扩散目标和取样器保持不变。

blocks.en:
Shared-weight recurrence increases effective depth without adding
parameters, building on Universal Transformers, equilibrium models,
and parameter-shared architectures ( Dehghani et al., 2019 ; Bai et al., 2019 ; Lan et al., 2020 ; Giannou et al., 2023 ) .
Recent work studies iterative computation, test-time scaling,
and the quality–compute trade-offs of recurrent depth ( Saunshi et al., 2025 ; Geiping et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ; McLeish et al., 2025 ; Prairie et al., 2026 ; Schwethelm et al., 2026 ) .
We investigate these questions in UDLM denoisers, including how
recurrent depth should be sampled during training.

参数,基于通用变换器,平衡模型,
和参数共享架构 (Dehghani等人,2019年;Bai等人,2019年;Lan等人,2020年;Giannou等人,2023年).
近期的工作研究 迭代计算 测试时间缩放
和重现深度的质量权衡(Saunshi等人,2025年;Geiping等人,2025年;Zhu等人,2025年;McLeish等人,2025年;Prairie等人,2026年;Schwethelm等人,2026年)。
我们在UDLM demoisers中调查这些问题,包括:
应在培训期间对经常性的深度进行抽样。

blocks.en:
Closest to our work, Lee et al. (2026) study recurrent depth
in masked diffusion, while related approaches explore recursive
blocks and fixed-point formulations ( Carballo-Castro et al., 2026 ; Miele et al., 2026 ) .
In standard absorbing masked diffusion, revealed tokens remain
fixed, whereas UDLMs must denoise observations of uncertain
reliability and can revise any token between diffusion steps.
We study whether recurrence remains effective under this
different corruption structure, and how its computation
should be allocated.

blocks.en:
Self-conditioning reuses clean-token predictions across
diffusion steps ( Chen et al., 2023 ; Strudel et al., 2022 ; Dieleman et al., 2022 ) .
Related approaches propagate latent states across steps or
introduce additional denoising recursion ( Jo et al., 2026 ; Suleymanzade et al., 2026 ; Yoo et al., 2026 ; Cameron et al., 2026 ) .
Our approach instead loops a slice of transformer blocks within each denoiser evaluation, updating hidden representations
while keeping the noisy sequence and diffusion time fixed.
These directions are complementary.

blocks.en: 7 Discussion and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 讨论和结论

blocks.en:
We studied the effect of looping in UDLMs by repeating a two-block slice of
the denoiser and training it with random loop counts. Looped models reach
the validation NLL of the non-looped baseline with up to 2.8 × 2.8\times fewer
training FLOPs on OpenWebText and 3.3 × 3.3\times fewer on FineWeb-Edu. We show
that at inference, looping lowers generative perplexity by up to 9.8 % 9.8\% at the same
NFE and zero-shot perplexity by 11.5 % 11.5\% on average. With adaptive looping,
the model needs 26 26 – 35 % 35\% fewer loop iterations on multiple-choice tasks
and keeps the same accuracy. Training on lower loop counts more often helps
further: on the same tasks, the model needs 12 % 12\% fewer loop iterations
than with uniform sampling, without degrading accuracy. We plan to extend
this study by comparing how looping helps masked and uniform diffusion,
especially on reasoning tasks.
